options.title: Why does the road from Alaska to Argentina stop in Panama?
options.first_line: Why does the road from Alaska to Argentina stop in Panama?
options.first_frame: A map of the Americas, one highway line drawn from Alaska down to Argentina, a car on it, and a red break in the line where Panama meets Colombia.

options.title: Why can nobody drive from Panama to Colombia?
options.first_line: Why can nobody drive from Panama to Colombia, the two countries right next to each other?
options.first_frame: Panama and Colombia side by side on the map, a car stopped at a road sign at the very end of the tarmac, green jungle beyond it.

options.title: The road from Alaska to Argentina has one gap. Why?
options.first_line: Try driving from Alaska to Argentina: one gap stops every car. Why is it there?
options.first_frame: A car at the top of a map in Alaska, a long road running down the Americas, a road-closed barrier standing at one point near the middle.

why: The whole Alaska-to-Argentina road with a red break at Panama is clear with the sound off, and it raises a mystery about a road anyone could drive without answering it, whereas B's jungle frame gives away the answer and C holds back where the gap is.
